lt_bots_education_body_howcreatedca_sing:
You can create a DCA bot by setting the following key parameters:

  • Price steps: defines the percentage difference at which safety orders will be executed. For example, if set to 1%, the bot will place safety orders at 1% price drops.
  • Take profit (TP) target per cycle: specify the percentage profit the bot should aim for in each cycle. When the bot achieves this target price, it ends the current cycle, completes the order, and starts a new cycle as specified.
  • Initial order amount: the starting investment amount for each cycle, placed by the bot to initiate the DCA strategy.
  • Safety order amount: the amount used for each safety order within a cycle. These incremental orders are placed at your configured price steps to lower the average entry price.
  • Max safety orders: determine the maximum number of safety orders the bot can place per cycle. The actual number depends on available funds.

Other optional parameters:

  • Amount multiplier: set a multiplier to increase the size of each subsequent safety order as the price moves against the initial order. For example, a multiplier of 1.5 will make each safety order 50% larger than the previous one.
  • Price steps multiplier: adjusts the price gap between each safety order. This setting incrementally increases or decreases the gap between safety orders as the price changes. For example, with a 1% initial price step and a multiplier of 2, the safety orders will be placed at 1%, 3%, 7%, and so on (doubling the gap after each order).
  • Stop loss (SL) price: another optional setting to limit losses. If the price drops to this level, the bot will stop trading and sell all base assets at the market price.
lt_bots_education_body_howcreategrid_sin:
You can create a spot grid bot by setting the following key parameters:

  • Lower price: the lowest price level at which the bot will operate. The bot will stop placing orders if the market price falls below this level.
  • Upper price: the highest price level at which the bot will operate. The bot will stop placing orders if the market price exceeds this level.
  • Grid quantity: this refers to the number of price levels (grids) that your selected price range is divided into. The bot will place buy and sell orders at each level. You can choose between arithmetic (evenly spaced grids) or geometric (proportionally spaced grids) distribution. Having more grids means the bot will execute smaller trades more frequently. Fewer grids result in larger trades but less frequent execution. For example, if the price range is 100-400, and you set the grid quantity to 3 with arithmetic mode, it would create three grids: 100-200, 200-300, and 300-400.
  • Grid mode:
    • Arithmetic: maintains a consistent difference between each grid level (e.g., 1, 2, 3, 4).
    • Geometric: maintains a consistent ratio between each grid level (e.g., 1, 2, 4, 8).
  • Investment amount: this is the total amount of the selected currency the bot will use to place buy and sell orders across the grids. The maximum amount is usually the available balance in your trading account for the selected currency.

Other optional parameters:

  • Take profit (TP) price: an optional price target. If the price reaches this level, the bot will stop trading and sell all base assets at the market price.
  • Stop loss (SL) price: another optional setting aiming to limit losses. If the price drops to this level, the bot will stop trading and sell all base assets at the market price.
  • Trailing up/down: this option allows the bot to automatically adjust the grid as the price moves, improving flexibility and maximizing capital utilization by adapting to market fluctuations.
lt_bots_education_body_howcreaterecurrin:
To create a recurring buy bot, you can set its main parameters as follows:

  • Crypto to buy and allocation: one or more cryptocurrencies to buy. If you want to buy multiple cryptocurrencies, set the allocation within which your bot will make purchases.
  • Frequency: you can buy hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly. For each frequency, you can specify exact purchase time.
  • Amount: the amount your bot will spend every time it makes a purchase.

You can also set optional parameters:

  • Buy price range: the range at which your bot will make purchases. It’ll skip purchases if crypto prices fall below the lower limit or rise above the higher limit.
  • Bot name: simply your recurring buy bot name to help you identify it.
lt_bots_education_body_howcreatesmartpor:
To create a smart portfolio bot, you can set its main parameters as follows:

  • Crypto allocation: cryptocurrencies and their percentages in your portfolio. You can set allocations manually, use equal distribution, or try smart distribution based on the crypto details and performance.
  • Rebalancing mode:
    • Proportional: rebalances your portfolio when the proportion of each crypto exceeds the threshold that you set.
    • Scheduled: rebalances your portfolio on a regular basis that you set.
  • Amount: the amount available for your bot to trade.
lt_bots_education_body_howdcaworks_prode:
A DCA bot aims to get the best average buying price and then sell crypto for a profit. It starts with a buy order at a specific price. If the price falls, your bot fills another buy order. This cycle repeats until you reach your maximum number of orders, take profit level, or stop loss level.

If you reach your take profit level, your bot starts another cycle from the first buy order. If you reach your stop loss level, your bot stops completely and won’t start a new cycle.
lt_bots_education_body_howgridworks:
A grid bot aims to buy crypto low and sell high to generate profit. When it starts, it spends portion of your trading amount to buy crypto depending on your trading range and the current price. It then places buy orders below the current price and sell orders above it at fixed trading levels. Intervals between these levels are called grids, and they form your entire trading range.

When crypto price reaches the next buy or sell order, it fills automatically. Your bot then places buy orders below the current price and sell orders above it once again. This way, you always buy low and sell high.

lt_bots_education_body_whatisbot_single:
Trading bots are automated software programs that execute trades on your behalf based on specific parameters and rules that are configured by you.

There are two types of trading bots offered on OKX — both come with risk that you should carefully consider before trading:

  • Spot grid bot: divides a price range into levels, buying low and selling high within this range.
  • Dollar-cost averaging (DCA) bot: buys more crypto if price falls, doubling down on each order and aiming to sell at a profit when the price rises.

Trading bots place orders directly on the main OKX spot order books, just like manual trades made on the platform. The bot uses the parameters you've set to decide when and how to place buy and sell orders based on real-time market conditions.

Please note that it’s your responsibility to ensure all bot settings are configured correctly, as incorrect inputs may result in unexpected outcomes. Trading bots don’t guarantee profits and carry inherent risks, including but not limited to the potential for losses due to market volatility and unforeseen market changes.
lt_bots_education_body_whatisdcabot: A DCA bot is a strategy that you can use to buy crypto at multiple price levels and then sell it for a profit. A DCA bot helps you get a better average buying price, because it automatically buys crypto when the price falls. It also automatically sells crypto when you reach your profit target.
lt_bots_education_body_whatisgridbot:
A grid bot is a way to trade automatically that you can customize and launch. It places buy and sell orders based on your input, so you don’t need to trade manually. The main idea of a grid bot is to buy low and sell high automatically.

The name comes from the grids — intervals between trading levels where orders are placed.
lt_bots_education_body_whatisrecurring: A recurring buy bot is an automated dollar-cost averaging (DCA) strategy. It automatically buys up to 20 different cryptocurrencies on a set schedule, averaging your buy price over time. DCA with a recurring buy bot mitigates market volatility and potentially helps you buy crypto at a lower cost. It also reduces market timing and emotional trading risks.
lt_bots_education_body_whatissmartportfo: A smart portfolio bot is a strategy that automatically manages and balances your crypto portfolio based on the preferences you set. If one crypto in your portfolio grows more than you want, your bot will sell some of it and buy more of the underperforming crypto to keep your portfolio balanced. A smart portfolio bot takes advantage of market fluctuations for potential gains. It’s a smarter and more dynamic portfolio management tool than simple holding.
lt_bots_education_body_whenbotstops_sing:
A trading bot will stop operating under the following circumstances:

  1. Based on your parameter settings: the bot will stop trading when it reaches specific conditions or thresholds you have configured:
    • Spot grid bot: if the price falls below the lower limit of the price range, the bot will stop placing new orders.
    • DCA bot: if the number of safety orders reaches the maximum limit, the bot will not place further orders.

    You can also configure stop-loss limits and profit targets which will automatically stop the bot once those orders are executed.

  2. Unpredictable circumstances: the bot may stop operating due to unforeseen circumstances that trigger OKX's Risk Management Stop (RMS) protocols, such as the delisting or suspension of the underlying cryptocurrency.
  3. Manual stop: you can manually stop the bot at any time by selecting the Stop button on the platform.

It is your responsibility to check on your trading bots regularly to see if any of them have stopped due to the above.

  • 价格下跌幅度不足，部分买入未触发。
  • 市场条件不允许，策略无法全部卖出。

当策略多次以 {takeprofitPercent} 止盈卖出时，总收益会随周期数增加。若买入后价格始终未回升，策略将无法卖出止盈。
